title: Six bids. Six formats.
job: Organic first, then paid. Over four weeks, post organic from the founder's personal LinkedIn profile, with the QSME page reposting each one: week 1 the reel (Hook 1), week 2 the carousel (Hook 4's framing on slide 1), week 3 the static, week 4 the Hook 2 binder static. This gives a directional read on which hook and format QSs and PMs comment on and share. Run the clean hook split (Hook 1 vs Hook 4) only in paid, as a 35s cut with the full ad anatomy, and boost the winning organic post as a Thought Leader Ad if LinkedIn supports that format. There is no real social proof yet, so the paid version relies on problem→solution and demo.
platforms: LinkedIn (primary), posted from the founder's personal profile and reposted by the QSME page: feed video (week 1), document carousel titled 'Six bids. Six formats.' (week 2), single image (week 3), Hook 2 binder single image (week 4)
LinkedIn Ads (only if organic shows signal): 35s video ad, Hook 1 vs Hook 4, Lead Gen Form with the 'Request demo' button; carousel as a document ad

YouTube Shorts (9:16 re-export; end card 'Book a 30-minute demo at qsme.build', large, held about 3.1s; title and description in Caption → SHORTS. Links in a Shorts description aren't clickable and a related-video link can only point to another YouTube video, so: point the channel header link at qsme.build, keep 'qsme.build' as plain text in the description, and set a related video only once a long-form QSME demo exists on YouTube. Posts only with a sound bed: see Production status → Sound bed)
Instagram / Facebook (optional cross-post: 4:5 static and carousel, 9:16 reel; IG CTA 'link in bio', FB full tracked URL in the caption)
core_joke_one_sentence: A deadpan QS counts through six bids for the same plasterboard & ceilings package (a PDF scanned sideways, a spreadsheet of merged cells, a lump sum 'as discussed', an email that says 'price below' with nothing below, the cheapest one that excludes ceilings on page 9, and a photo of a whiteboard), decides the whiteboard was the most complete bid of the lot, then admits their own tender email just said 'drawings attached, please price.'

hooks.mechanism: Mid-action start (deadpan count), made readable with sound off
hooks.text_layer: Large, top third: '6 bids. 6 formats.' Small chip: 'Tender closed 5:00pm'. Counter '0/6' top-right. The six banners on the foreground phone are each stamped '4:59 pm'.
hooks.visual_layer: Frame 1: a phone propped in the soft-focus foreground. Six generic 'New message' banners (subject 'Tender – Plasterboard & ceilings', each stamped 4:59 pm, no OS or app logos) stack down its lock screen 0.15s apart. Behind it the QS, already mid-sigh at their own desk in window light, stares into the lens, with the six bids fanned out in front of them. Focus racks from the phone to their face on 'Six formats.'
hooks.audio_layer: Six generic message pings within about 1s, synced to the banners (not an Outlook or iOS sound), then dead silence as they speak
hooks.why: Every QS and PM knows tender close. With sound off there are now four layers: the big text, the banners that make the pings visible, the everyone-at-4:59 joke, and the rack focus. The 0/6 counter keeps people watching to see what #6 is, and the whiteboard stays the peak of the escalation. 'Subbies' stays out of the VO until the markets are confirmed (open question on qsme.build markets).

hooks.verbal_layer: (one beat of silence) "...This is a tender submission."
hooks.visual_layer: A phone photo of the whiteboard bid (marker prices, flash glare in one corner, half-erased site sketch) slid into a clear sleeve labelled 'TENDER – PLASTERBOARD & CEILINGS – BIDDER F' and clipped into a ring binder
hooks.audio_layer: Marker squeak, then a binder ring snapping shut
hooks.why: The strongest single frame, but it spends the punchline in second 1. Used as the week-4 single-image static, captioned 'This is a tender submission.', after the reel, carousel and static have run. It could be a paid hook test later. Never the reel opener.

hooks.visual_layer: Bid E's total circled in red pen. A highlighter drags down the page to a tiny asterisk, then a snap to page 9: '*Note 14: Excludes ceilings.'
hooks.audio_layer: Room tone, then one highlighter squeak
hooks.why: Every QS has been burned by the cheapest bid's fine print. The on-screen asterisk carries the joke with sound off, and the package name ('& ceilings') makes the exclusion land. No countdown graphics, so it stays UGC. It uses up Bid E's beat, so it works as a standalone short or a later paid hook test, not as the reel opener.

hooks.text_layer: 'Unpopular opinion: the best bid was a photo of a whiteboard.'
hooks.visual_layer: The QS holds the phone up to the lens showing the whiteboard photo, completely straight-faced. The five 'proper' bids sit in a neat, ignored pile beside them.
hooks.audio_layer: Room tone only; one pen click at the end of the line
hooks.why: High curiosity (why would that win?), and it takes the subbie's side from second 1. At 6 words (about 2.4s) it is trimmed to exactly 2.5s like Hook 1, so the body starts on the same frame. In this variant only, the 6/6 VO becomes the callback 'And yes… the whiteboard.' and the snap-zoom onto 'CEILINGS … INCL' does the work. Its framing, without the reveal, gets an organic read as carousel slide 1. The paid A/B challenger.

hooks.verbal_layer: Speakerphone, cheerful: "Did you get my price?" QS, staring at the phone: "I got… a photo. Of a whiteboard." Speakerphone: "Yep. Ceilings are in."
hooks.visual_layer: Phone on speaker lying on the desk. The QS looks at the photo, then slowly at the camera.
hooks.audio_layer: Ringtone cut off mid-ring, compressed speakerphone voice
hooks.why: Rewritten so the subbie wins the exchange, and 'Ceilings are in' calls back the cheapest bid. It needs a second voice (a real person, or a clearly fictional ElevenLabs voice). Parked as a part-2 post told from the subbie's side, not the reel hook.

chosen_reason: Hook 1 (mid-action count, index 0). Tender close is a ritual every QS and PM has lived through, so this LinkedIn audience recognises it instantly. With the stacking 4:59 banners, the big '6 bids. 6 formats.' text and the rack focus, it now reads with sound off, which is how LinkedIn autoplays. The 0/6→6/6 counter keeps people watching, and the whiteboard is saved for the peak rather than spent in frame 1. Hook 4 (contrarian) is the paid A/B challenger and gets an organic read through carousel slide 1.

music.direction: No music under the six-bid count or the self-own. Deadpan needs dead air, so each bid gets one small real sound instead, recorded on set where possible. Music enters only at the product beat (21.5s) as a tidy, minimal pulse that feels like rows snapping into line, then resolves on a single chord under the end card. No trending track and no stock 'corporate ukulele'. Duck it about 18 dB under speech.
music.mood: Dry and understated, quietly satisfied: order after chaos
music.bpm: 90–100 BPM (suggest 96) for the 8.5s solution/CTA cue; a 17s version for the paid cut, which enters at 18.5s
music.source: ElevenLabs Music on a plan that covers commercial use: a 10s instrumental, e.g. 'minimal clean plucked synth and soft kick, 96 BPM, understated, no vocals, resolves on one chord at 8.5s', plus a 17s version for the paid cut. Alternative: a licensed stock-music library on a plan that explicitly covers business/brand channels and paid social ads (not a personal or creator tier); add the LinkedIn page and ad account if the licence requires channel registration. SFX: record paper, trackpad, highlighter, marker and cap sounds live on set; generic message pings from ElevenLabs Sound Effects.
music.licensing_note: LinkedIn has no licensed music library for posts, so anything posted there, organic or paid, needs music you hold rights to: generated, or licensed stock music on a commercial/brand plan. IG/FB business accounts are generally limited to Meta's commercial Sound Collection for organic posts, and trending songs are not cleared for brand or ad use. Paid ads on any platform: generated or commercially licensed only. CapCut is for cutting and captions only: no CapCut library music, sound effects, AI voices, stickers or templates, because these are often not cleared for commercial use. Confirm the ElevenLabs plan includes commercial use before using its music or VO in ads.

voice.character: 'The QS who's seen every spreadsheet horror': a mid-career quantity surveyor (late 30s to 40s), calm and dry, never raises their voice, amused rather than angry. Quietly on the subbies' side, and honest enough to admit the tender email was theirs.
voice.accent_and_delivery: If the founder or a real QS films, use their own natural accent and wording; don't coach it. The AI VO uses a natural, general urban New Zealand accent (the user confirmed Kiwi for both QSME NZ and qsme.build on 2026-10-02; see ventures/qsme-build.md), never broad, never Australian, no American hype. vo-script.md is the timed source for the VO. Delivery is the same either way: flat deadpan, unhurried, short sentences. A real half-second pause before 'a photo of a whiteboard', a tiny wince on 'In fairness…', and the only warmth on 'Honestly? Most complete one here.' Never an announcer read, including the CTA.
voice.elevenlabs_direction: Only for the no-person version (Figma kinetic type + VO). Voice Design prompt: 'Mid-career quantity surveyor, around 40, general urban New Zealand accent, not broad, low-mid register, dry and deadpan, slightly tired but amused, conversational, close to the mic like a phone recording, no announcer energy.' Generate 3 candidates and keep the least polished one. Use Eleven v3 for audio tags such as [sighs] and [pause] (check the current tag list). Starting settings: stability about 45–55, similarity about 75, style exaggeration 0–15, speed about 0.95. Example lines: 'Six bids. Six formats.', 'And one… [pause] is a photo of a whiteboard.', 'In fairness… [pause] mine said "drawings attached, please price."' An AI voice must not present itself as the founder, so the product line becomes 'Next tender: one schedule. Every bidder gets the same lines.' instead of 'So we built QSME.' Render each line separately, 3 takes per line, so the edit controls timing. Note the chosen voice ID in ventures/qsme-build.md. Never clone a real person's voice without their explicit consent (the founder cloning their own voice is fine).
voice.real_person_alternative: Recommended for LinkedIn: (a) the founder on camera at their own desk. They perform the skit and deliver the product half as themselves ('So we built QSME. Same lines for every bidder.' and the CTA). (b) A real QS who isn't a QSME user performs only the skit (0–21.5s). The product beats are then screen recording plus on-screen text, or the founder's voice-over, never the QS's voice on product or CTA lines. Add a paid-partnership disclosure if they're paid, and get a simple written release. Either way: phone, window light, about 30–45 minutes to film. ElevenLabs then supplies only the pings and music.

production_workflow.what: The user picks the hook (recommended: Hook 1, with Hook 4 as the paid challenger), decides who's on camera, answers the open questions, and says yes before anything costs money. Estimate: about 2h for props and printing, 45min shoot, 2h edit. Spend: one month of an ElevenLabs paid plan with commercial use, plus printing. No AI video spend if a real person films.

production_workflow.what: Timestamped script where the captions are the VO word for word, the 8 carousel slides, the static copy, the four captions (reel, carousel, static, binder), the 35s paid script, and one UTM link per asset

One file, 'QSME Build – Six quotes', using the brand tokens from ventures/qsme-build.md (#0C1310, #3DC023, Space Grotesk SemiBold, Inter, logo at ventures/assets/qsme-logo.svg). Cheers.', a long empty scroll and 'Sent from my phone'; the QS's own sent email ('Tender: Plasterboard & ceilings package / Drawings attached. Please price.'); six generic notification banners stamped 4:59 pm with no OS or app logos; a sticky note 'F'; the binder sleeve label for Hook 2. Frames: static 1080x1350, carousel 8 × 1080x1350, lower-third, end card.

production_workflow.what: Write Bid F on a real whiteboard to the spec (itemised boards and ceilings lines, 'Ceilings … INCL' underlined twice, jointing incl, access incl, validity 30 days, total + tax). Photograph it on a phone with the glare and half-erased sketch in one corner, clear of the lines. Then shoot two overhead flat-lays on a real desk in window light: all six face-up (static), and Bid F face-down with the sticky note 'F' (carousel slide 1). Also shoot the binder shot for Hook 2.

Static: the solid #0C1310 band across the top 22% with kicker, headline and green subline; the photo below; labels of three words or fewer at 32px or more. Carousel: real photos in the frames, counters top-right, the whiteboard inset crop on slide 6, the 'Compare bids' totals crop (6 bidders, excl./incl. tax, 'Lowest') on slide 8. Export the carousel as a PDF titled 'Six bids. Six formats.' for LinkedIn and as PNGs for IG/FB.

production_workflow.tool: QSME demo project (fictional data) + Mac/iOS screen recorder
production_workflow.what: Owner records these (signed-in screens), one UI state per clip, punched in at 2–3x with a slow push-in: (1) the bidder's view of the tender: the same lines, rate column empty (ideally split-screen with the owner's priced SOQ); (2) 'Compare bids' with six demo bids: totals excl./incl. tax, 'Compare on' toggle, 'Lowest' tag; (3) click a bid → 'Award bid' → the contract with milestones and retention (Active Work); (4) Agreements: 'Make the agreement' → 'Send for signing'; (5) estimate → tender cut from it (for slide 7 and the paid cut). The comparison is totals only: never film or describe a per-line grid of every bidder's rates. On a Global (non-GST) demo, check the labels first (they may still say GST).
production_workflow.output: 3 clips of about 4s usable each, 1080p or higher

production_workflow.tool: Phone (founder, or a real QS for the skit only)
production_workflow.what: Shoot 9:16 at eye level, window light, real desk, natural accent, uncoached. 3 takes per line plus inserts: the foreground phone with the rack focus to the face (phone Cinematic/portrait video mode, or a blur ramp in the edit); the sideways PDF rotate; the spreadsheet sort click and alert close; the 'price below' empty scroll; the page flick + highlighter; the whiteboard phone reveal; the laptop turned to the lens with the sent email; writing '6 bids. 1 schedule.' and capping the marker. Record the real paper, trackpad, highlighter and marker sounds on set.

One Figma frame per beat, using the real prop photos, big type and the counter. Animate with Smart Animate and export as MP4 (the connected Figma integration lists a video export tool; test it on one frame first, and fall back to screen-recording the prototype). The VO follows the ElevenLabs direction, with the product line 'Next tender: one schedule. Every bidder gets the same lines.' Use Higgsfield/Runway/Veo only if a human on screen is truly needed and nobody will film: a fictional QS, not a testimonial, AI-labelled where required. Not recommended for LinkedIn.

SFX: six generic message pings, plus any sound not captured on set (no cartoon sounds). Music: a 10s cue (organic) and a 17s cue (paid), 96 BPM, resolving on one chord. Check the plan covers commercial use.

Cut tight and start late. Burned-in captions are the VO word for word, large enough to read with sound off, and double as the subtitles: no separate subtitle track, no SRT, and LinkedIn auto-captions off at upload if offered. Only the top-right counter 0/6→6/6, with no '1/6 ·' prefixes. The 0.5s snap-zoom on 'CEILINGS … INCL' at 16.5s. Music in at 21.5s, ducked under speech. No CapCut library music, SFX, AI voices, stickers or templates; all audio comes from the set recording and the ElevenLabs stems. Export 1080x1350 for LinkedIn and 1080x1920 for Shorts/Reels, with 9:16 text between y=300 and y=1400 and more than 150px from the right edge, and the end card held at least 2.5s.

Watch with sound off: does the hook read in under 3s? Check every claim against the research file ('gets the same lines', 'never see your rates or budget', 'award creates the contract'). No real brands, logos, OS UI, names or client data. Check that the subbies aren't the butt of the joke and the self-own lands, and that nothing shows or claims a per-line grid of every bidder's rates (the live screen compares totals). Third-watch test: is it still funny?

The user posts from the founder's personal profile and the QSME page reposts: week 1 reel, week 2 carousel, week 3 static, week 4 binder static. The founder posts the first comment with their own true strangest-quote story (not written by us); the tracked link goes in a separate comment. UTMs: qsme.build/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=six-quotes&utm_content=reel-h1 (then carousel-h4, static-whiteboard, static-binder; utm_source=instagram/facebook for cross-posts). After 7 days per post, log impressions, comments, reposts, average watch time (if LinkedIn shows it) and demo bookings by utm_content. Winner = highest (comments + reposts) per 1,000 impressions, with at least 1,000 impressions; a video must also average at least 10s watch time. Treat organic results as directional only.

production_workflow.what: 35s cut from the same footage. 0–2.5 Hook 1 or Hook 4 (both exactly 2.5s). 2.5–13.5 bids 1–5 as in the organic reel. 13.5–17.0 the whiteboard + snap-zoom (Hook 4 variant VO: 'And yes… the whiteboard.'). 17.0–18.5 'Honestly? Most complete one.' 18.5–21.5 product intro: lower-third 'QSME · tendering & estimating software', VO 'QSME fixes the tender, not the subbies.' over estimate → tender. 21.5–25.5 value: VO 'Price the estimate once. Every bidder gets the same lines.', on-screen 'Bidders never see your rates or budget.' 25.5–29.0 demo: VO 'Six bids. One table. Award creates the contract.' over 'Compare bids' (totals excl. tax, 'Lowest') → 'Award bid' → contract with milestones and retention (no e-sign step on Global). 29.0–35.0 CTA at the whiteboard: VO 'Send one schedule, get six bids you can actually compare. Book a 30-minute demo at qsme.build.' End card: 'Book a 30-minute demo at qsme.build'. About 85 words; the founder voices the product lines. Run it as a video ad with a Lead Gen Form ('Request demo'), and the carousel as a document ad. A/B Hook 1 vs Hook 4 with everything else fixed. Boost the winning organic post as a Thought Leader Ad if the format supports it. Set a fixed test budget before launch. Judge hooks on video view rate and 25%/50% completion, then CTR and cost per demo request.

integrity_notes: Product claims come only from the research file and venture profile, and are worded to match: 'tendering & estimating software'; one estimate with every tender cut from it, so every bidder gets the same lines ('prices the same lines' waits until the bidder flow is confirmed); bidders never see your rates or budget; bids compared as totals excl. and incl. tax in one table with a 'Lowest' tag (each bid opens to its own lines); award creates the contract with milestones and retention, and the agreement is then sent for e-sign. Never say or show a per-line grid of every bidder's rates: that matrix exists only on an unmerged branch. 'The contract's already made' was removed.

Still dropped until confirmed: 'same tax basis', automatic exclusion detection, and 'lowest conforming bid'. The page-9 exclusion is shown only as the problem. The live comparison shows totals only, so there are no per-bidder line rows to show blank, and nothing implies 'QSME catches exclusions'.

No social proof anywhere: no customer counts, logos, time-saved figures, star ratings or testimonials. 'Six bids', 'page 9', 'note 14', 'rows 12–40', '4:59' and the whiteboard rates and totals are props inside the skit, not data.

Who speaks: the founder may say 'So we built QSME' and the CTA because they are the company. A real QS who isn't a user performs only the skit and never voices product or CTA lines; disclose a paid partnership if they're paid, and get a written release. An AI voice never presents itself as the founder.

First person: the captions open with the generic 'Every QS has had this tender close.' and make no claim that a specific tender happened. First-person lines ('mine said…', 'here's what I sent them') live only inside the clearly staged skit and carousel. 'We've all sent that one' assumes the poster is a QS; if the founder isn't, change it to 'Most tender emails look like that.'

The joke is aimed at the situation and at ourselves, not at subbies (who are qsme.build users): the whiteboard bidder wins, the QS admits their own tender email caused it, and the paid line is 'QSME fixes the tender, not the subbies.' Hook 5 was rewritten so the subbie wins, and it's parked.

No real brands or identities: generic spreadsheet (no Excel logo or ribbon), generic mail UI, generic alert and generic notification banners (no OS or app branding, no Outlook/iOS sounds). Bidders are labelled 'Bidder A–F' with no company names. No real projects, addresses or client tenders. Screen recordings use a demo project with fictional data. For the NZ twin, any 'Facebook group' screen must be a generic community-group UI (neutral grey, no logo, made-up group name, no Facebook colours, layout or reaction icons).

Any AI-generated QS must be fictional, must not resemble a real identifiable person, must not be framed as a testimonial, and must be AI-labelled where LinkedIn/Meta rules require. Flag this to the user before using one.

Audio rights: no trending or chart music on LinkedIn or in ads; generated or commercially licensed music on a brand/ads-cleared plan only; no CapCut library audio, voices, stickers or templates. No voice cloning of a real person without their explicit consent.
Comment seeding: the founder's first comment must be a true story of their own. We don't write one for them.

Owner CTA rule (2026-10-03): the only CTA is 'Book a 30-minute demo at qsme.build' (end card, VO, captions, static, carousel, paid cut). No pricing generosity of any kind (the banned phrases are listed in ventures/qsme-build.md, CTA rule) on screen, in the VO, captions, hashtags, titles or thumbnails. Checked 2026-10-04 across post.md, post.json, vo-script.md/json, the motion sources and the Figma scripts.
Nothing gets generated, spent or posted until the user approves the hook and the spend. The user does the posting.

'Same lines for every bidder' is true. Still open: can they attach exclusions to specific lines?

~~In the comparison view, do unpriced lines show as blank?~~ Answered: the live comparison is a table of totals (excl. / incl. GST, 'Lowest'), one bid opens at a time to its own lines; the per-line grid across bidders is branch-only. Still open: does the iOS app show the comparison (for a portrait-native recording)?

Brand tokens and the logo are in ventures/qsme-build.md (pulled from the site 2026-10-02). Is there an existing Figma file or library to use instead? Is there a demo project with fictional data we can screen-record?
Humor limits for qsme.build: is joking about quote formats OK now that the post takes the subbies' side and the QS takes the blame?
ElevenLabs: does your plan include commercial use (needed for music and VO in ads)?
Want the NZ twin next (qsme.co.nz, 'The Facebook group' idea, Kiwi VO, FB/IG) built with the same workflow, and Hook 5 as a part-2 post from the subbie's side?
